title: post-edit-diagnostics: spawnSync('tsc') cannot resolve the .cmd shim on Windows — the entire TS/JS diagnostics path is silently dead on the primary platform, and the early return also skips the bus 'edited' write for every TS/JS edit

evidence.quote: 1. **`.cmd`/`.bat` shims CANNOT be spawned directly on modern Node (CVE-2024-27980 hardening).**

causal_links: causes D2e-08 partially (TS/JS edited-role rows missing from intel-bus files_in_play)
observe_how: ls of C:/Users/david.hayes/AppData/Roaming/npm and .claude/hooks/node_modules/.bin shows only tsc (sh), tsc.cmd, tsc.ps1 — no tsc.exe. Node spawnSync on win32 resolves only .exe, so result.error (ENOENT) fires and the hook prints '{}' BEFORE recordBusFilesInPlay (line 255). The project's own C.1 platform contract documents this exact trap; user CLAUDE.md still claims '*.ts/*.tsx edits trigger automatic tsc --noEmit diagnostics' — a decision-driving false claim. Fix per windows-platform.md finding #1: invoke the real JS entrypoint (node <pkg>/typescript/bin/tsc) or cmd.exe /c tsc.cmd with array args, and hoist recordBusFilesInPlay above the early returns.
telemetry: intel-bus: 318 live rows but TS-heavy sessions show edited-role gaps; zero tsc diagnostics ever injected on this machine

title: HYBRID_FLOOR 0.01 is applied to decay-multiplied RRF scores, mathematically excluding most of the memory corpus from proactive injection

evidence.quote:
const TEXT_ONLY_FLOOR = 0.05;  // FTS ts_rank scores: 0.05-0.5 typical
const HYBRID_FLOOR = 0.01;     // RRF fused scores: 0.01-0.03 typical

# Keep the legacy "similarity" key in sync so existing consumers
        # that read result["similarity"] see the decay-adjusted score.
        r["similarity"] = base * weight
DEFAULT_DECAY_LAMBDA = 0.02

COALESCE(1.0 / (${rrf_k_param} + f.fts_rank), 0) +
                COALESCE(1.0 / (${rrf_k_param} + v.vec_rank), 0) as rrf_score,

observe_how: Math is fixed by the constants: with rrf_k=60 the max single-arm RRF score is 1/61=0.0164 and max dual-arm rank-1 is 2/61=0.0328. The JSON `score` the hook floors is similarity=base*decay (decay=exp(-age_days*0.02)). Solving 0.0164*exp(-0.02a)>=0.01 gives a<=24.7 days; 0.0328*exp(-0.02a)>=0.01 gives a<=59.4 days. So ANY single-arm match older than ~25 days and ANY match at all older than ~59 days is silently dropped, regardless of relevance. The floor comment assumes pre-decay RRF scores; the value floored is post-decay.
telemetry: table-memory-recall.json: top_score p75=0.0149 (just under single-arm 0.0164 max), p50=0, hit-rate 27.4% — consistent with a corpus mostly older than the 25/59-day cutoffs.
